description: Self-contained grade rubric. Runtime selects one of the three genres in this file.

rubric.notice: Project-authored common rubric reconstructed from public sources. Not an official US rubric, an equating function, or a validated educational assessment.

task_content.1: Meaningful text exists, but response to the assignment or relevant development is very limited.
task_content.2: Addresses part of the assignment; ideas/support are uneven, general or partly irrelevant for the selected grade.
task_content.3: Addresses the assignment with clear relevant ideas and sufficient grade-appropriate development/support.
task_content.4: Develops the assignment purposefully with well-selected details/support and insight within the selected grade expectations.

organization.1: Relationships or sequence are hard to follow; needed boundaries/connections are largely absent.
organization.2: Some organization is visible, but gaps, repetition or weak connections interrupt the progression.
organization.3: Ideas/events follow a coherent grade-appropriate sequence with suitable connections and opening/closure where expected.
organization.4: Purposeful ordering and effective varied connections strengthen the text as a whole; boundaries fit purpose and grade.

language_expression.1: Imprecise or repetitive language makes the intended meaning difficult to follow; little suitable control of expression.
language_expression.2: Language conveys some meaning, but vocabulary, sentence patterns or tone are uneven or poorly matched to the task.
language_expression.3: Vocabulary, sentence choices and tone communicate clearly and suit the grade, genre and audience.
language_expression.4: Deliberate precise language, effective sentence choices and consistent tone enhance meaning without unnecessary complexity.

conventions.1: Frequent grade-relevant grammar, spelling or punctuation difficulties repeatedly obstruct meaning.
conventions.2: Partial control of grade-relevant conventions; recurring errors distract or occasionally obstruct meaning.
conventions.3: Adequate control of grade-relevant conventions; minor errors generally preserve meaning and readability.
conventions.4: Consistent control of grade-relevant conventions in a sufficient text sample; rare minor errors do not distract.

scoring_rules: Judge each domain independently using the selected CCSS grade/band and genre overlay. Give concrete textual evidence in feedback.
The levels are ordinal project anchors; they are not empirically calibrated cut scores. Level 3 denotes the stated target, not an official proficiency classification.
Score 4 means effective use within the requested grade, never mandatory older-grade skills. Score 1 is limited performance, not absence of all ability.
Assess development/support in task_content, structure in organization, stylistic choices in language_expression, and correctness in conventions. Avoid counting the same defect repeatedly.
Source-use scoring concerns fidelity and attribution; quality of reasoning/support remains in task_content.
No universal minimum word count, paragraph count or advanced-vocabulary quota. Short age-appropriate K writing can be scorable.
Off-topic or off-purpose writing can receive a low task_content score while other domains are assessed from the actual text; do not automatically mark it entirely unscorable.
Do not infer motivation, personality, oral fluency, handwriting, collaborative effort, actual research process or external source credibility.

anchors.1: Source-based information is largely unacknowledged or distorted; substantial copying is not distinguished from the writer’s own wording.
anchors.2: Some sources are identified, but attribution, paraphrase/quotation fidelity or task-required documentation is inconsistent.
anchors.3: Sources are identified at an age-appropriate level; paraphrases/quotations preserve meaning and required documentation is adequate.
anchors.4: Source attribution is clear and unobtrusive; accurate paraphrase/quotation and complete task-appropriate documentation distinguish borrowed material effectively.

source_use.applicability: Only when supplied source passages exist and the genre is not narrative; otherwise not_applicable and null, not zero.
source_use.grade_guidance: Use clear source identifiers and faithful paraphrases/quotations; require a source list only if the assignment asks for it.

rubric.not_scorable_policy: Project policy: abstain only when the text cannot support evaluation of the core domains, or is not sufficiently English for this English-writing task. No fixed length threshold.

normalization.meaning: Position on an ordinal project rating scale, not percent correct, mastery percentage or cross-grade ability.

rubric.total_policy: No aggregate score or cross-grade ranking; source_use not_applicable is excluded rather than treated as zero.
scope_notes: Student-authored text only; no drawings or adult-transcribed speech.
Grade-relative descriptors do not make equal numbers equivalent abilities across grades.
Mock validates contracts and routing, not writing quality or human-rater agreement.

genre_overlay.task_content: Develop a claim using relevant evidence and reasoning. Acknowledge and distinguish opposing claims.
genre_overlay.organization: Judge connections between claims, reasons and evidence; include counterclaims only as required by the selected grade.
genre_overlay.language_expression: Use precise topic language and formal style.

standards.notice: Project paraphrases of selected text-observable Writing and Language standards, not the full curriculum. No inference about revision, collaboration, handwriting, speaking or research process.

standards.CCSS.ELA-Literacy.W.8.1: Introduce claims and distinguish opposing claims; organize logical reasons and relevant evidence from accurate credible sources, connect claims/reasons/evidence/counterclaims, maintain formal style and conclude.
standards.CCSS.ELA-Literacy.L.8.1: Use verbals and active/passive or conditional/subjunctive forms appropriately; avoid inappropriate voice/mood shifts.
standards.CCSS.ELA-Literacy.L.8.2: Use commas/ellipses/dashes for pauses, ellipses for omissions and correct spelling.
standards.CCSS.ELA-Literacy.L.8.3: Use verb voice/mood deliberately for particular effects.

genre_overlay.task_content: Explain a topic using facts, definitions, details or examples appropriate to the selected grade. Do not require a position or counterclaims.
genre_overlay.organization: Group related information with grade-appropriate links and closure; advanced grades clarify relationships among complex ideas.
genre_overlay.language_expression: Use precise explanatory/domain vocabulary and task-appropriate tone; a narrative voice is not the target.

genre_overlay.task_content: Develop events, characters or experiences with grade-appropriate details and techniques. Reward relevant narrative development instead of argumentative evidence.
genre_overlay.organization: Judge event progression, time/setting transitions and closure against the selected standards. Establish point of view as required by the selected standards.
genre_overlay.language_expression: Assess descriptive/sensory language, dialogue or sentence choices where useful. Do not require every narrative technique or formal academic tone.
